observations.body: Paul is hailed, stoned, and rises in Lystra. At Lystra a certain man sat, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked. But as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city. On the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.

payload.posture: Read Acts 14:8–20 as one movement in Paul's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states paul is hailed, stoned, and rises in Lystra. At Lystra a certain man sat, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked. But as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city. On the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Paul's story.
